51573862.DESCRIPTION: Binding affinity to FXR (unknown origin) assessed as dissociation constant by surface plasmon resonance assay
51573862.references_previous: 35. X. Wang, R. Yang, S. Liu, Y. Guan, C. Xiao, C. Li, J. Meng, Y. Pang, Y. Liu, IMB-XMA0038, a new inhibitor targeting aspartate-semialdehyde dehydrogenase of Mycobacterium tuberculosis, Emerg. Microb. Infect. 10 (2021) 2291–2299.

original_paragraph.Materials and Methods - 4.3.11. Surface: The SPR assay was performed on a Reichert2SPR system (Reichert, New York, USA) at 25 °C using CM5 chip. CM5 chip was coated with purified FXR in 10 mmol/L sodium acetate buffer at pH 4.5. The binding of FXR at different concentrations (6.25–50 μmol/L) of compound 3a was performed in 1 × PBST (Thermo Scientific) at a flow rate of 25 μL/min for 90 s, followed by dissociation for 150 s. The results were analyzed using TraceDrawer software (Reichert, New York, USA) [35].
original_paragraph.Figure 6I plot description: The sensorgram in Figure 6I shows the response (in RU) over time (in seconds) for compound 3a at concentrations of 6.25, 12.5, 25.0, and 50.0 μmol/L. The x-axis ranges from 0 to 300 seconds, with the association phase from 0 to 90 s and the dissociation phase from 90 to 240 s. The y-axis (Response) ranges from 0 to 20 RU. The curves show increasing response with higher concentrations, with the 50.0 μmol/L curve reaching the highest response (~15 RU).
